A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same UniQL research work, with complete readable main text and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching of equations, algorithms, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, compression-time, latency and ablation experiments in Sections 4–5, with additional benchmark, energy and pruning analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and the additional evaluations and analyses in Appendices B–F.

M1.justification: Structured weight sorting, quantization-aware SVD, state-aware compression, masked LoRA fine-tuning and adaptive pruning remain unchanged. Algorithms 2–3 and their accompanying MHSA explanation are repositioned without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Alpaca and WikiText2 data and retain the five zero-shot tasks, MMLU and MBPP+ evaluations. Architecture coverage and cloud/edge test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MoDeGPT, SVD-LLM, TRT-AWQ, TAO-HQQ and GPTQ. Appendix B also retains the same ShortGPT-Alpaca, SliceGPT-Alpaca and MoDeGPT-Alpaca comparison rows; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Shot counts, batch sizes, calibration settings, training budgets, pruning configurations and profiling procedures are unchanged. Appendix E/Table 16 corrects 'Js/req.' to 'J/req.' for the already-defined joules-per-request measurement.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same fused-RoPE, fine-tuning, decomposition, calibration-data and 3-bit ablations. The Pareto, energy and layer-wise pruning analyses in Appendices D–F are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report average latency over twenty profiles after five warmup runs. Neither adds or revises seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outcomes are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 4 retains 71.4% for 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B at 15% pruning, and Table 16 retains 143.12 J per request for Qwen-2.5-7B at 35% pruning.

T1.justification: The block formulations, sorting-score definitions, SVD derivations and quantization equation remain unchanged, as do the mathematics in Appendices A and F. Moving the MHSA material across pages 5–6 introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified compression, one-shot processing, configurable on-device pruning and efficiency across Transformers, SSMs and hybrids. Abstract edits correct wording without changing claim scope.

C2.justification: Explanations of quantization compatibility, numerical instability, accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and hybrid-layer sensitivity are retained. Applicability qualifications, the Qwen Hadamard exception and the impact statement are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix G retain the same implementation information, calibration sample counts, LoRA hyperparameters, Hadamard configurations and hardware details. The code/model access statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. UniQL's positioning relative to compression, quantization and elastic-training methods remains the same.

P1.justification: v3 corrects the abstract's redundant 'large language model (LLM) models,' makes small wording and hyphenation edits, and removes the ONR Minerva acknowledgment. The MHSA explanation is consolidated before its algorithms, while the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Algorithms 2–3 are grouped on page 6, with Figure 4 moved below them. Figure 2 receives spacing and label edits, and Table 16's caption and headers correct the energy-unit notation. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability by keeping the MHSA explanation uninterrupted before Algorithms 2–3 and Figure 4. Correcting 'Js/req.' to 'J/req.' in Appendix E/Table 16 also improves notation. These are limited presentation gains; the methods, empirical evidence and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
